code_constants.value: Echo shows the next note after a 0.55-second interval; after a completed verse it waits 0.7 seconds before replaying the next verse, and a wrong note waits 0.9 seconds before replay (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5880-5892,5917-5929).
code_constants.scope: Source intervals only; no child-visible cadence or rendered timing was observed.
Three coded rounds; not a measure of total play time.

timing.assumptions: No gameplay time was observed. Isolated probe wall time does not measure a play session.

tactile.target_size: Echo stars are centered at 22%, 50%, and 78% of surface width and 52% of height; drawing uses 54-pixel radius (64 while lit), with nearest-star acceptance only within 92 pixels (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5865,5894-5905,5950-5958). Actual screen projection, target separation and hit alignment on Lenovo Tab M11 are unknown.
tactile.press_response: During listening, a correct tap lights the selected star and advances input; a wrong star asks the stars to replay (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5906-5929). The assigned probe did not establish visible response latency or voice playback.
tactile.drag_hold_release: Echo is discrete press/tap input; no drag or hold is required in _echo_press (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5894-5931). Release behavior and ordinary GUI event routing were not established by the assigned headless run.
tactile.ownership: The mechanic is tap-based and this review found no focused assertion establishing multi-touch ownership for echo. One-finger live input is the expected route, but no physical touch was tried.
tactile.cancellation: No focused echo cancellation, pause, focus-loss, or re-entry behavior was verified in this invocation.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: listening to a short star phrase and choosing its notes gives a preschooler a clear listen-then-answer role, with no punishment on a wrong answer. Whether the cue is understandable without coaching remains unobserved.
play_appeal.variety: The three verses change from two notes to three, then reverse order; the following encore changes the verb to drawing a circle (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:114; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:343-347). This is source variety, not observed child interest.
play_appeal.world_response: Correct notes produce a star glow and the assembled-song row grows after each verse; a wrong note restarts the phrase instead of ending play (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5907-5929,5950-5965). The probe log does not establish how readable or encouraging this looks or sounds on device.
play_appeal.replay: The source repeats a missed verse and then offers the encore phase. Hypothesis: the replay may feel supportive if the child notices the glowing cue; observed replay choice is absent.
play_appeal.concrete_test_or_proposal: In a short consented child observation, play one verse without coaching, then allow a wrong tap and one retry. Record whether the child waits for the stars, taps the lit sequence, notices the replay after a miss, and independently chooses to continue to the encore. If the wait feels inert, test a more apparent visual countdown/glow cadence while keeping wrong answers harmless and requiring the child's taps for progress.

play_sequence.input: From the visible Opera Hall route, choose Pop Star and enter the lesson; do not assume the probe's direct setup proves this route.
play_sequence.wait: Allow the welcome cue and arrival to finish before touching the lesson surface.
play_sequence.basis: Opera Hall lists Pop Star among its three venue careers (scripts/opera_house.gd:120-123); venue route remains unobserved here.

play_sequence.input: Complete the Pop Star practice phases using the visible prompt: hold the microphone, tap the glowing dance arrow, then tap the noisy band when cued.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for each current phase cue and its response before the next input; no duration estimate is asserted.
play_sequence.basis: Practice phase definitions and instructions are scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:229-235.

play_sequence.input: At RHYTHM, keep hands still while the first two-star phrase plays.
play_sequence.wait: Wait through the shown phrase and for the listening cue; notes are scheduled 0.55 seconds apart (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5877-5892). This is code timing, not measured play cadence.
play_sequence.basis: Echo SHOW mode lights notes before listening; scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5880-5892.

play_sequence.input: Tap the two lit stars in order, then wait and tap the three-star phrase in order.
play_sequence.wait: After each completed phrase, wait for the next phrase to begin; code uses 0.7 seconds (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5917-5923).
play_sequence.basis: Verse arrays [0,2] and [0,1,2], with correct taps advancing one note at a time (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:114,5907-5925).

play_sequence.input: Wait for the final reversed phrase, then tap its notes in the displayed/sung order.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the listening cue before each answer; no real-time measurement was made.
play_sequence.basis: The final source verse is [2,1,0] and the probe's focused echo checkpoint leg restores the first note before accepting the second (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:114; scripts/probe_opera_performance.gd:303-343).

play_sequence.input: If a note is missed, wait for the stars to replay and try the phrase again; do not coach the child during the observation.
play_sequence.wait: Code replays a missed verse after 0.9 seconds (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5923-5929); this is not observed child pacing.
play_sequence.basis: Wrong-note path restarts the verse without a fail state (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5923-5929).

play_sequence.input: After RHYTHM completes, follow the ENCORE cue by drawing one big circle, then let the child choose whether to replay or leave.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the phase result and choice; no total duration or reward timing is claimed.
play_sequence.basis: Stage RHYTHM and ENCORE have echo/circle modes and short verbal cues (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:343-347).

observations.title: Pop Star stage adds a three-round echo song after its practice lessons
evidence: scripts/opera_performance_plan.gd:8,16-34 enables popstar, duplicates each source phase into practice and stage, and sets stage_start to the practice count.
scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:343-347 defines stage RHYTHM as echo with three goal units and ENCORE as circle.
scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:335-428 checks approved venue careers and performance phase structure; runtime/L22/attempt_1/probe.log ends OPERA2D|result: ALL OK.
observations.reproduction: Inspect the Pop Star source phase list, then follow OperaPerformancePlan.build: the first three source phases are copied to practice and source phases are copied again as stage phases. The assigned probe passes its broad Opera assertions but does not simulate a child choosing this route.
observations.child_impact: A familiar tap/hold/dance lesson transitions to a listen-and-repeat song, adding a changed activity before the encore. Whether this feels like a rewarding performance or an overly long repeat is unknown.
observations.proposed_repair: No repair is justified from these assertions. Observe a child-paced session first and retain the short repeated phrases if the child understands and opts in.
observations.acceptance_test: On the target phone from a fresh save, verify that visible Pop Star practice leads to exactly the intended stage phases and the child can independently reach and complete the echo and encore without reading.

observations.title: Echo phrases grow and change order, and wrong taps trigger a gentle replay
evidence: scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5907-5929 advances correct input and restarts after a wrong note without a failure state.
scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5950-5965 draws the current lit star and cumulative song row.
observations.reproduction: Trace _echo_press for one correct note and one wrong note. The wrong note resets echo_show_i and schedules replay; no focused child-facing run occurred in L22.
observations.child_impact: This can teach that mistakes are safe and the song changes, but the child must notice when to listen and when to answer. Comprehension and encouragement are untested.
observations.proposed_repair: Keep the harmless replay. Only adjust cue timing or visual contrast if device/child observation identifies a specific missed cue.
observations.acceptance_test: Observe an uncoached non-reader through a correct phrase and one intentional wrong note; verify they wait for the replay and can retry without confusing the song with their turn.

observations.title: Echo uses discrete taps with an explicit nearest-star cutoff
evidence: scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5865 sets star centers; 5894-5905 selects the nearest of three only within 92 pixels.
scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5950-5958 draws 54-pixel stars, enlarged to 64 when lit.
observations.reproduction: Compare the star center/radius drawing to the 92-pixel nearest-input radius. This establishes base-canvas code geometry only; there is no rendered capture or touch test in this review.
observations.child_impact: Forgiving taps may help a one-finger player; the 92-pixel cutoff can still reject a tap that appears close depending on canvas scaling and device alignment.
observations.proposed_repair: No code change without observed evidence. Capture the stage at required aspect ratios and measure visible star-to-hit alignment on device.
observations.acceptance_test: At target device and approved aspect ratios, tap star centers and edges plus the intervening gaps; confirm each intended star responds within two rendered frames and visually separate stars do not select ambiguously.
